crossStackDependencies.reason: The gauge implementation reuses InstrumentKey introduced by the counter-description commit and does not compile against the frozen baseline alone; port feca160d first.

reviewerNotes.note: This incremental ledger starts with the audit's only patch-equivalent commit; remaining commits stay intentionally unclassified until bounded subsystem review supplies semantic evidence.
Stable patch-id 1a064aa40b799932dfce02b52ee3b25d0510ee3e maps upstream 9e0d7f02c9416c46dde6e571068a0fb03a4facdf to local 15f0bf854bf82de2eaf3524f089dc8efaa88a307.

The first #418 batch reviews two adjacent plugin-cache changes together, but they remain separate rows because local curated cache pruning and remote global catalog listing have no shared symbols or semantic dependency.

The second #418 batch keeps analytics privacy, advisory configuration, and MCP API hygiene in separate rows because they share no symbols or implementation dependency. Future MCP tightening must retain the public new_uninitialized_with_permission_profile constructor used by codex-core.

The third #418 batch records the OTEL counter-description and gauge primitives as separate missing rows so partial future adoption remains visible. The gauge row depends on the counter row's InstrumentKey, and later in-range exec-server lifecycle metrics consume the same description-aware foundation.

riskFlags.reason: codex_error_subreason still serializes up to 512 bytes of InvalidRequest text into analytics, including raw provider bodies; remove the field and transient copy before treating the checkpoint as adopted.

rows.rationale: Local commit 83c14c3676b6ecae9d717b3a869e806087685b93 predates the frozen implementation baseline and adds RUSTSEC-2026-0173 to both .cargo/audit.toml and deny.toml. Its shorter comments preserve the same proc-macro-error2 dependency path, temporary suppression, and removal intent, so the upstream behavior is already adopted.

The frozen audit marks this as the range's sole patch-equivalent commit. Both commits produce stable patch-id 1a064aa40b799932dfce02b52ee3b25d0510ee3e and change the same eight files with identical behavior: canonical auto_review output, legacy guardian_subagent input, and active reviewer propagation into delegated agents.

The baseline TurnCodexError copies CodexErr::InvalidRequest text, bounds it to 512 bytes, stores it as subreason, and emits codex_error_subreason in codex_turn_event; serialization tests assert the field. Upstream removes that free-form telemetry path because InvalidRequest can include raw provider bodies or user-derived text. The bounded copy is mitigation, not adoption, so the privacy hardening remains missing.

The baseline refresh_curated_plugin_cache checks the active cache version before marketplace membership and only warns when a configured plugin source is absent. It has no raw marketplace name loader, cache uninstall path, or removed-plugin regression test. The behavior is applicable local cache hygiene and leaves user configuration untouched.

The baseline writes the global remote catalog cache after a synchronous fetch and uses cached entries for recommendations, but plugin/list always awaits fetch_remote_marketplaces and has no cache-presence check or background-refresh option. The optimization is applicable, with future implementation preserving Every Code's existing auth-isolated cache key and remote route.

The baseline and current metrics client cache counters only by String and expose no InstrumentKey or counter_with_description API. Upstream adds description-aware instrument identity without changing existing counter callers, and later in-range exec-server lifecycle metrics consume counter_with_description. The reusable foundation is applicable, low-risk, and missing.

The baseline keeps list_available_server_infos and new_uninitialized public even though their only non-definition callers are inside codex-mcp and its tests. The upstream API hygiene is applicable but absent. A future focused port should narrow those two methods without importing method-order-only churn and must leave new_uninitialized_with_permission_profile public because codex-core calls it in production.

The baseline and current metrics client have no Gauge import, gauge cache, i64_gauge construction, gauge methods, or gauge export tests. Upstream reuses InstrumentKey from feca160d, making that row a compile-hard dependency, and later in-range lifecycle metrics retain the gauge foundation while adding observable callbacks. The gauge primitive is applicable and missing.
